Done, one execution, no failures.

**Approach:** plain script on `safetensors` + `torch` (`out/T1/solution.py`). It reads the sharded input through `model.safetensors.index.json`, skips blocks 2/6/10/14, and builds a *new* dict under the renumbered names — so the collision hazard never arises, and any duplicate new key would abort.

**Checks enforced before anything is written** (all `sys.exit(1)` on failure):
- no `model.layers.{12,13,14,15}.*` remains
- exactly 12 `self_attn.q_proj.weight` matches, indices exactly 0..11
- 7 tensors per block, 86 tensors total, both non-block tensors present
- every surviving tensor compared bit-exact (shape, dtype, `.equal`) against its source under the old name

**Result:** `out/T1/model.safetensors`, 86 tensors, 12 blocks. Report written to `out/T1/REPORT.md`. I chose a script over mergekit because the drop set isn't a contiguous range (mergekit passthrough would need four slices plus a model-level re-export) and this is a pure key rename where bit-exactness matters.
